ownership_reason: Only the gold reads the entries of the source map and decides how each is added to the receiver (the entry's collection of values for a multi map, the entry's value otherwise); hops 1-4 pass the receiver and the source map along unchanged. The gold's javadoc promises that every value of the specified map is added to the collection stored against its key; for the trigger's MultiValueMap source the values are object1 and object2 (MultiValueMap.values: the combination of values from all keys; MultiValueMap.totalSize counts them), and the variant adds the collection [object1, object2] as a single value instead. No one-line change of the two arguments above the gold restores the values: the gold puts each entry's value as one element and no Map handed to it can hold two values for one key. The convention is pinned outside the gold: AbstractMultiValuedMap.putAll(MultiValuedMap) copies a multi-valued source by calling put(k, v) once for each mapping from key k to value v (MultiValuedHashMapTest testPutAll_Map1: 4 values, 3 at "key"); MultiValueMap.putAll(Object, Collection) adds each value of a collection at its key (MultiValueMapTest testPutAll_KeyCollection); MultiValueMapTest testValues counts six values for three keys; the facade's own javadoc says a multi map's entries are added using putAll(Object,Collection).
